name: Metallic Seaweed
lede: Metallic Seaweed is a dark, inky teal, named for wet seaweed's sheen rather than its usual dull green-brown.

sections.title: The shine, not the color, of seaweed
sections.body:
Seaweed itself runs from olive-brown to deep green; the name here points at the slick, almost metallic reflection wet seaweed carries in sunlight, not at its ordinary hue [1]. Our library carries this color from Wikipedia's extended color lists, with no further paper trail, so an exact coiner and date are undocumented in the sources checked here [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[capri-blue]] and [[deep-aqua]], the first almost identical, the second a touch greener [1]. [[ocean]] and [[ming]] sit a little further off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 23 of 23,781 paintings, 0.1 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 6 [2]. That makes it rarer than 73 percent of the named colors we track [2]. The earliest dated painting with it is from 1505, by Gerard David, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2].
